I am a 73-year-old farmer in Dongmaliangu Village, Anzhai Township, Quzhou County. After fifty-five years on this land and with a high-school education, I know every corner of my twelve mu. My wife and I are the only laborers, so we must be efficient. We are fortunate to have a reliable well for irrigation. This year I will stick to what has always worked: eleven mu in the wheat–mazie double crop for grain security, and one mu of cotton for cash income.

For **winter wheat**, I will rotary till the eleven mu and sow the improved variety *Liangxing 99* in early October. I will spread 150 jin per mu of special compound fertilizer—18 % nitrogen, 22 % phosphorus, and 5 % potassium—as a basal dressing. With our well water I will irrigate three times: once in winter to protect against the cold, and twice more at jointing and grain filling. Aphids and powdery mildew are regular threats here, so I will spray five times for insects, twice for weeds, and once with fungicide. I expect about 1,000 kg per mu come early June.

Immediately after the wheat harvest, I will sow **summer mazie** *Denghai 622* on the same eleven mu using no-tillage. This hybrid yields well and saves precious labor between the two crops. I will apply 150 jin per mu of compound fertilizer containing 28 % nitrogen, 6 % phosphorus, and 6 % potassium. I will irrigate twice during silking and grain filling, and spray three times for insects plus once for weeds. I am counting on roughly 1,232.5 kg per mu by early October.

On the remaining **one mu of cotton**, I will rotary till and sow the improved variety *Lumianyan 27* in early April. I will lay plastic film to conserve heat and moisture, and apply 100 jin per mu of compound fertilizer with 20 % nitrogen, 10 % phosphorus, and 21 % potassium. Cotton is thirsty and prone to bollworm, so I will irrigate twice and spray insecticide thirteen times and herbicide twice. I also apply growth regulator twice to keep the stalks from growing too tall. I expect about 500 kg of seed cotton per mu by late October.

This plan balances our food supply, cash income, and what the two of us can realistically manage.
